title: Failed Agent Requests Recorded with Status Code 500
dataSources: Trace `status_code` set by `conclude(conclude_all=True, status_code=500)` in the request handler's exception path
description: Makes sure a request that raises an exception still reaches Splunk Agent Observability as a concluded trace with `status_code=500`, instead of being lost or merging into the next request's trace.
value: Failed requests are the ones an investigation needs most. Recording them with a 500 status keeps them countable by the Status Code alert (UC-13.8.10) and stops a batch loop from attaching the next request's spans to a still-open trace.
implementation: Wrap the request handler so any exception calls `conclude(conclude_all=True, status_code=500)` and `flush()` before re-raising. Test the path offline with `ingestion_hook` so the real stream gets no junk traces.
visualization: Agent Stream trace table filtered to status code 500.
knownFalsePositives: Client-side validation errors that the agent handles and answers normally are not failures and should not be marked 500.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

Wrap the request handler. On exception call `conclude(conclude_all=True, status_code=500)` and `flush()` before re-raising. Otherwise the trace is lost, and in a batch loop the next request's spans can attach to the still-open trace.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

In the Agent Stream trace table, filter or sort by status code to see failed requests next to their span trees.

Step 3 — Validate

Test the exception path offline with `SplunkAOLogger(ingestion_hook=captured.append)` and assert `captured[0].traces[0].status_code == 500`. Then force one failure against a test stream and confirm the trace shows status 500. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Pair this with the Status Code alert (UC-13.8.10) so a rise in 500s notifies the owning team.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Spans from two requests in one trace: an earlier request left its trace open. Check every exit path of the handler concludes with `conclude_all=True`. Missing failed traces: the exception path raised before any agent span was added, so the trace had no spans (see UC-13.8.2).
grandmaExplanation: When the assistant trips over a problem, we still write down what happened and mark it as failed, instead of losing the note.
